description: HyperI default Renovate preset. commitMessagePrefix is fix(deps): DELIBERATELY -- semantic-release's default rules release on fix/feat/perf and nothing else, so a chore(deps): bump lands on main and never ships. The stack deploys by digest, so an unreleased bump is an undeployed one, and the security PRs this preset works hardest to raise early were the ones that never reached production. Releases do not multiply: semantic-release batches every commit since the last tag into one version, so the only NEW releases are the cycles where dependencies were the only change -- which is the gap. Ship a security patch the same way, as fix(security):.

customManagers.description: Backing-service image tags pinned in our own source. testcontainers module libraries ship HARDCODED default image tags (Rust's Kafka default is confluentinc/cp-kafka:6.1.1 from 2021, Redis 5.0 from 2018), and a tag baked into a dependency's source is invisible to every manager -- Renovate reads Cargo.toml, correctly reports the crate current, and never sees the image. Testcontainers for Java, .NET and Node have all deprecated their defaults for this reason; Rust has not, so we pin in our own code and annotate it here. The convention is a `renovate:` comment followed by a BARE TAG on its own line (KAFKA_TAG = "4.3.1"), never embedded in the image ref -- RE2 has no lookahead, so picking the right colon out of "${VAR:-name:tag}" is not something one pattern can do reliably. Covers Rust consts, Python constants, shell variables and CI scripts with one regex. See hyperi-ai plans/2026-07-29-deps-version-parity.

packageRules.description: Security/vulnerability fixes bypass the COOLDOWN (PR raised immediately, not after 7 days) but are still PR-only - a human merges the CVE patch now.

Same-org HyperI packages bypass the cooldown - we publish these ourselves, supply-chain risk for our own packages is governed by our own CI gates and release process, not by external-attacker cooldown logic. Matches anything whose source URL points back to github.com/hyperi-io/* - crates.io, PyPI, npm, GitHub Actions, plus any GHCR images that set the org.opencontainers.image.source label (which the hyperi-ci container handler does by default).
Same-org HyperI container images bypass the cooldown - backstop for any ghcr.io/hyperi-io/* image that didn't get the source label set (which would otherwise miss the matchSourceUrls rule above).
Group all GitHub Actions updates (PR-only, like everything else)
Group Rust crate updates

Rust bumps must MOVE a version, not just raise a ceiling. Cargo's default rangeStrategy is `auto`, and the manager docs say auto picks `widen` whenever the range carries a 'less than' instruction and `update-lockfile` otherwise -- so our own house style of writing explicit bounds (vrl = '>=0.33.1, <0.34') is precisely what selects widening. The result is a PR that edits Cargo.toml alone and never touches Cargo.lock: nothing resolves differently, the build is byte-identical, and CI goes green having compiled the OLD version. dfe-transform-vrl#24 (2 lines) and dfe-archiver#35 (3 lines) were both exactly that, and a widened 0.x ceiling silently admits a BREAKING line into the next `cargo update`, which is how the `cel` bump got in. `bump` raises the range to start at the new version and updates the lockfile with it, so the thing CI compiles is the thing the PR proposes.
Group Python dependency updates
Group TypeScript/Node dependency updates
Group Go dependency updates
Group Docker image updates

Group the customManagers pins -- the backing-service tags annotated with a `renovate:` comment in our own .rs/.py/.sh source. Every group rule above matches on a BUILT-IN manager, and a custom manager is none of them, so these arrived one PR per dependency: dfe-receiver and dfe-transform-vector each got their own vectordotdev/vector PR for the same upstream binary, with nothing making the pair land together. Custom managers share one identity (`custom.regex`) regardless of how many are declared, so a single rule covers the lot. The old spelling was a bare `regex`; anything before Renovate 37 will not match this.

Group the Kubernetes and infrastructure-as-code pins. The docker group covers dockerfile and docker-compose only, so helm chart deps, helm values and OpenTofu/Terraform providers fell through it and arrived one PR per dependency -- dfe-infra alone carried separate PRs for curl, vault, otel-collector and clickhouse-keeper. There is no OpenTofu-specific manager; `terraform` reads .tf either way.

Kafka CLIENT and BROKER bump together, in ONE PR. They are not independent knobs: testcontainers' module encodes a per-image wait strategy and broker port (the Confluent module exposes 9093, the Apache one 9092), and librdkafka supports a protocol range. Split across two PRs you get an intermediate state where the client and broker disagree and the integration tests are the only thing that would have told you. Grouping them makes that suite gate the COMBINATION, which is the only real proof the pair works.

ClickHouse CLIENT and SERVER bump together. Server defaults move between majors and surface as client failures: from 25.x the entrypoint refuses to leave `default` passwordless unless told, and a client that assumed otherwise just gets 'Authentication failed' with nothing naming the version.

AWS SDK and the S3-compatible servers we test it against bump together. SDK-side signing and checksum changes are a recurring MinIO/LocalStack compatibility tripwire, and the failure looks like a broken test rather than a version pair.

testcontainers and every image it supplies a default for. The crate's wait strategies are written against specific image output -- its OpenBao path waited for 'Vault server started', which OpenBao does not print -- so bumping the crate without the images, or the reverse, breaks container startup with a message that names neither.

ClickHouse stays on the LTS line. dfe-infra's versions.yaml picks 26.3.13.31 deliberately (24.8 past-EOL, 26.3.14/15 too fresh at the time) and dfe-engine writes DDL against that server. Gating versions.yaml alone was not enough: nothing parses that file, so the SSoT looked protected while the SAME image pinned in a compose file, a CI script or a chart values file was wide open. That produced dfe-infra#32 (keeper to 26.7, four minors ahead of its own server), dfe-engine#117 (CI to 26.7 while tests/integration/conftest.py stayed on 26.3) and dfe-loader#94 (26.6 -- the exact off-LTS version the 2026-07-16 unification moved AWAY from). Constrained rather than disabled so patches WITHIN the LTS line still flow: gated must not mean unwatched. Widen this bound when the estate moves to a newer LTS, deliberately and in lockstep with the operator.

Kafka cannot exceed what the operator runs. Strimzi 0.51 supports 4.1.x/4.2.0, so 4.2.0 is a hard ceiling and anything above it is a broker the operator will refuse to reconcile. dfe-infra records this against services.kafka-version; this rule makes it hold everywhere the image is pinned, not just in the SSoT file. Verify against strimzi's kafka-versions.yaml before widening.

Redpanda tracks the operator chart's tested pairing, not the newest tag. dfe-infra pins v26.1.8 as the broker the operator chart 26.1.6 pairs with. Left open, Renovate proposed v26.1.14 and v26 on the compose side of repos whose PGO workload already ran v26.1.8 (dfe-loader#95, dfe-archiver#37/#34), so the two pins for one broker drifted apart. Constrained to the 26.1 line so patch bumps still flow.

Python baseline for the whole suite. requires-python is '>=3.12', which is a FLOOR and reads to Renovate as permission to offer anything newer -- it proposed python:3.14-slim for dfe-engine (#36). That image would not start: the builder stage produces a 3.12 venv and `COPY --from=builder /app /app` carries it into the runtime, where pyvenv.cfg names a missing interpreter, site-packages sits under lib/python3.12, and every compiled extension is cp312 ABI. The suite moves off 3.12 together, deliberately; widen this when it does.

hyperi-ci's OWN reusable workflows float @main on consumers (always-latest CI) - Renovate must NOT pin or bump the caller. SHA-pinning exists for THIRD-PARTY + project deps; pinning our own CI tool's version at the consumer just makes consumers miss CI fixes (they stuck on stale SHAs). Safety for @main is the internal interface gate (hyperi-ci issue #31), not a consumer pin. Deliberate pins (a chosen @vN, or @sha for a known reason) are still allowed - this rule only stops Renovate from imposing one. Last rule so it overrides helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests + the github-actions group above.
